P1.evidence: No setter on this call so no notes to read back. Frame was three-part, not four: 'You just want to get a good idea where you're at, you know, build out what it is that you want to accomplish, and then if everything aligns, we can talk about the coaching' — no 'what's in the way' or 'what you need'. Agreement was sought and given ('All righty?' / 'Yeah'). The open question was replaced by the prospect volunteering ('I could probably make that really simple for you') and the rep saying 'Go on, then. Hit me.'

P2.evidence: Baseline was barely run. No age, height or weight taken at all on a fat-loss call. Work was covered well, including whether he is on the tools ('I'm not on the tools. I'm in upper management') and the 12-15 hour days. Diet was asked directly ('What's your diet like? What kind of stuff you eat?'). The C5/C6 and stenosis were volunteered under a routine question, never asked for — a miss under the rule that the script credits asking. No sleep, no energy, no results-from-current-training. Training capacity was asked forward-looking ('Can you make four days a week, 45 minutes?') rather than establishing actual days trained.

P3.evidence: Surface goal was asked cleanly: 'if we were to fast forward six months, like what's it really that you want to achieve?' and got body weight plus moving better. The rep then closed the topic himself — 'I got you man, that's as simple as that, it's simple for you hey' — and never bridged to why. No 'what's driving this right now', no impact-on-others, no kids/marriage/legacy, no reflect-back. A prospect with a partner, a house build and a 15-hour-day job had obvious depth available and none of it was taken.

P4.evidence: 'What do you struggle with in terms of putting it back into a routine?' is a clean P4d and produced the injury and the routine gap. Past attempts (Keith Weber videos, Instagram sets) were volunteered rather than asked for, and the rep never asked why they did not stick — the prospect diagnosed himself: 'I've just got to have to think, just lacking the discipline.' The rep affirmed the structural read informally ('You've got into the habit of not doing it and that's like the norm now') but did not run 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own?'

P5.evidence: No two-year consequence question, no 'willing to settle', no 'why not'. The only move in the neighbourhood was 'Do you feel like you're ready then to actually make a change?', answered with a flat 'Yeah, of course'. The rep also supplied the consequence himself ('it sounds like you're fed up of it') rather than making the prospect say it, so there was no emotional cost on the table when price landed.

P6.evidence: No commitment check of any kind before the offer. The rep went from 'Can you do four days a week, 45 minutes?' directly into the structure and then the price at 00:11:07. Neither 'do you believe you can get there with the right structure and the right person in your corner' nor 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in' was asked. This is the phase whose absence explains the outcome: the partner objection surfaced after the price, with no prior yes to return to.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted ('Alrighty, what do you want to do brother?') but the prospect deferred to his partner, so payment, the Trevor onboarding booking, the agreement email and the Skool/welcome-email steps were never reachable. The rep did correctly state the sequence — investment first, then the onboarding call with Trevor — when asked.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger: 'the only thing was the cost that was higher than I was expecting.' The rep did not isolate ('finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%'), did not use the should-I/how frame, and asked none of the financial-picture questions — cash on hand, monthly surplus, cards, available credit, investments. He ran one reframe ('it gives you 8,388 reasons why you're going to stick to it this time') and later volunteered the split-payment option unprompted, which is the last move of the play used first and without the permission question that is supposed to precede it.

Trigger: 'I'll have to have a discussion with my partner... we would need to discuss first as a family.' The rep got her name and asked a version of 'when you talk to her, what obstacles might come up?' via 'What do you think she'll say? Do you think she'll be on board or do you think she'll be not on board?'. He never asked 'money aside, do you personally feel this can get you there', never asked whether this is genuinely her input or permission to bet on himself, never used the not-a-joint-decision-like-a-house frame — notable given the prospect literally is buying a house — and never offered the deposit-plus-refund fallback. He accepted the deferral and set a WhatsApp callback.

Timing was raised in substance: 'it's just looking at that forecast... we've got a lot going out the door in the next six months' and 'there's a fair bit until we crack dirt in October with this build'. No OD move was run. The prospect actually pre-empted it himself — 'I was about to say if it was a couple of months' time, but I don't want to do that. I'd rather get going' — and the rep did nothing with the opening beyond 'Well, that's the right attitude.'

Clinical fit. The prospect disclosed C5/C6 injury propagated into spinal stenosis with nerve compression down the arm. There is no scripted play for this and the rep improvised a reassurance ('with your C5, C6, you [want] to make sure that's getting all better as well'; 'First month is always mastering the form... don't want to go back to 34 kilo snatches'). No clearance question exists anywhere in the script for the rep to reach for. Script gap, not solely a rep failure.

notes: The whole middle of the process was skipped: no baseline numbers, no deep why, no consequence frame and no commitment check before a price was named at eleven minutes. That is why an experienced, motivated, well-funded prospect who said 'I'd rather get going' still left on a partner conversation — there was no agreed stake for the price to be measured against. Coach the commitment check first; it is the single change that would most likely have converted this call.
